key_insight: Combining 3D welding simulations with neural networks identified a favorable HDPE friction stir welding window at 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process selection to reduce void defects, moderate thermal gradients and stabilize axial forces in HDPE joints.
method: Simulate temperature, force, material flow and defects using a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force responses.
Combine simulation and neural-network predictions to map defective and defect-free process windows.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation showed ANN R² values of 0.91–0.99, while 60 °C bottom preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N.
watch_item: Prediction reliability outside the tested process range remains unestablished; new materials or operating conditions require validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
